outcome: An off-site immutable copy of your critical systems, held under separate credentials nothing in production can reach or delete.
overview: Regulators and insurers increasingly expect an off-site immutable copy that a compromised production environment cannot reach, and building one on-premises means a second facility. Veeam Data Cloud Vault provides that copy as a managed cloud service with immutability and access separation from the customer’s own cloud accounts. The design questions worth pressing on are which copies go to the vault, how long they stay immutable, and how quickly they can come back — because egress and restore time are what make a vault usable or merely compliant.

benefits.text: An off-site immutable copy exists without building or operating a second facility
benefits.limits: The vault is operated by the vendor; the customer’s own compliance position on that arrangement must be established rather than inherited

benefits.text: Access separation means a compromised production or cloud account cannot delete the vaulted copy
benefits.limits: Separation protects against deletion; it does not detect that vaulted data was already compromised before it arrived

benefits.text: Vault cost is predictable because storage and egress are priced within the service
benefits.limits: Backup success rate is not recoverability; only a tested restore against a stated objective evidences it, and the two are routinely substituted for one another

residency: The vault is a vendor-operated cloud service; its region is selected at design and is the decisive question for a regulated customer

notFor.situation: A bank whose supervisor requires the last-resort copy to remain in a facility the bank controls
notFor.why: This is a vendor-operated service; where that is not acceptable, it is not a candidate

notFor.situation: An estate with no immutability anywhere in its protection design
notFor.why: A cloud vault as the only immutable copy leaves the primary estate unprotected against the same attack

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Veeam implementation partner · Duration: 4–8 weeks to a replicating vault with a timed restore test
Support model: Vendor service support for the vault; Redington coordinates the vendor case and the review cadence.
1) Review — copy set, retention depth against detection time, residency and supervisory position
2) Design — replication schedule, credential separation and restore test plan
3) Configure — vault provisioned, replication running, immutability verified
4) Test and hand over — timed restore test at a representative volume, schedule handed over
deliverables: A delete attempt using production credentials against a vaulted copy fails, demonstrated rather than described
A restore from the vault completes and its time is measured at the agreed representative volume
The reported restore time states the volume it was measured at and what it does not imply
effort: 4–8 weeks to a replicating vault with a timed restore test
